# HogNoise

> Procedural noise for Python (Perlin, OpenSimplex2, cellular/Worley, value, white noise, fractals, domain warp): the FastNoiseLite and FastNoiseSIMD algorithms in one package, rendered two ways (numba and numpy, bit-identical) from one parameter record and checked against committed vectors from the originals. The `pyfastnoiselite` binding is a reference used only when asked for. A GPU rung runs every noise as one WGSL compute shader through wgpu (the `gpu` extra), only when asked for: `make_sampler(params, backend="wgpu")` or `HOG_NOISE_BACKEND_NOISE=wgpu`. It is float32, held to a measured per-feature tolerance at frequency 0.01 out to 4,096 units, not bit-for-bit with the CPU, and not benchmarked. The same shader ships as naga's HLSL, GLSL 4.30 and SPIR-V, with the tables and a binding manifest, read through `hog_noise.shaders` (standard library only); each compiles in its own language's tools, none has yet been run against the vectors by a host, and there is no Metal. 2D and 3D only; no 4D yet. Pre-release, installed from GitHub.

Use it when someone wants seeded 2D or 3D noise over numpy arrays: terrain and heightmaps, textures, games tooling that must match FastNoiseLite (Godot 4, Unity, C++), a replacement for `pyfastnoisesimd`, or noise in a DCC host's Python. For 4D, a node editor or C++ speed, FastNoise2 is the better answer.

## Evidence

- [vectors/portability.md](vectors/portability.md): every comparison, with its largest difference
- [vectors/portability-gpu.md](vectors/portability-gpu.md) and [vectors/tolerance/wgpu.json](vectors/tolerance/wgpu.json): the GPU rung against every hog feature on four adapters, and the bounds derived from that measurement
- [vectors/README.md](vectors/README.md): the reference vectors' format, and how any port checks itself against them
  (`python -m hog_noise.conformance vectors --rendering numpy`)
- [packages/python/hog-noise/src/hog_noise/shaders/README.md](packages/python/hog-noise/src/hog_noise/shaders/README.md): the emitted HLSL, GLSL and SPIR-V, their bindings per language, the dispatch and the uniforms
- [Docs/noise/GALLERY.md](Docs/noise/GALLERY.md): every noise type rendered
- [Docs/findability.md](Docs/findability.md): who this is for and why they would want it
- [Docs/decisions/ADR-007-noise-kernels-port.md](Docs/decisions/ADR-007-noise-kernels-port.md): why a port, and the measurements behind the choice
